figures.caption_en: Archived cost and output audit, retaining all unfavorable cells. (a) Arithmetic mean cumulative scheduling plus nonempty result-processing time per run (five processes); colors use a logarithmic seconds scale. This is not single-cycle latency or total CPU utilization. (b) Shared-case confirmed executed positions; hatch denotes repeated positions. (c) Exact-sequence/completed counts against matched Native; the starred Native row is a reference identity, not an independent exactness test. Different sequences remain visible even when token counts agree.

figures.caption_en: Frozen drain-trigger comparison on 48 new identities reused across 24 processes. (a,b) Lines join each distinct input cohort under D=64 (open) and D=256 (filled); upper labels give SLO-qualified/16 counts and lower labels the cohort-time percentage change. Cohort dispersion is not repeated-run uncertainty. (c) Pooled completed requests divided by summed process time, with pressure circles and roomy squares. Four of six direct D64/D256 pairs have output differences; these are complete-configuration sensitivities, not a scheduling-only causal effect or cross-GPU balancing result.

figures.caption_en: Client-observed two-engine trajectory on one RTX5090. All times and cumulative counts come from the exact derived trajectory, not invented raw events. Gray denotes offered-to-admitted waiting; worker colors denote admitted-to-final-delivery intervals. The gold right axis counts final deliveries. This is not internal token-kernel timing or heterogeneous-GPU speedup.

figures.caption_en: Constructed ownership diagnostic from six 12-request runs. (a) Points give gain/recorded-snapshot percentages; connecting segments span the two measured settings and are not uncertainty intervals. (b) Exact numerators and denominators preserve unequal snapshot counts. The 58 correlated gain observations represent 11 distinct positive rank-labeled states; no independent-snapshot inference is made. All 72 requests, including the 36 EOS-enabled requests, stop at their caps.

figures.caption: Archived backend-latency proxies on separate hosts and configurations. Rows identify GPUs and columns model sizes; vector cells show completed-request medians in milliseconds and record counts n. A single global color scale is used. Hatched cells mean not recorded, not zero or failure. These are neither streaming TTFT/TPOT measurements nor a matched heterogeneous-serving comparison. The repeated scaling view is omitted without removing any measured cell.

figures.caption: Supporting CPU calculations and controlled policy execution, not GPU-serving benchmarks. (a) Median reserve-reduction arithmetic across archived settings; shaded bands show setting minima and maxima, not confidence intervals. (b) Actually executed routing at alpha=0.025 and zero label noise, with the expectation alpha*T/2 as a dotted reference. (c) Label-noise control at T=10,000. Panels (b,c) retain all 20 seed observations as open points and display means with sample SD. Queue, Locality, Flat collapsed and Typed no residual coincide exactly; TypedRoute and Flat sufficient coincide exactly. Coincident methods are grouped only after checking every corresponding archived record. No curve is a live heterogeneous-GPU result.
